# Manufacturing Demand Forecasting — Plant-level planning with dynamic AI models

Generated July 26, 2026 — Sales Brief

Leading building-materials manufacturer — A Blend360 Case Study

## Executive Summary

Blend360 replaced a slow, short-horizon Excel forecasting process with a client-owned platform that combined financial history, external market indicators, automated model refreshes, and scenario planning. The solution extended the planning horizon, increased granularity to individual plants, and materially reduced forecast error. ([(LongForm)_180_Manufacturing_Data Science & Insights_Supply Chain_Demand Forecasting.pptx])

## The Challenge

The existing Excel tool took five minutes to open, was difficult to extend to new facilities, relied on basic statistical methods, and produced only a three-month business-unit forecast. It did not incorporate external economic factors or align cleanly with workforce planning. ([(LongForm)_180_Manufacturing_Data Science & Insights_Supply Chain_Demand Forecasting.pptx])

## Our Solution

Blend360 developed an end-to-end forecasting platform that integrated financial history with macroeconomic indicators, projected monthly demand and P&L line items at plant level, supported economic what-if scenarios, and exposed model investigation and approval through a Streamlit interface. The client owns and operates the solution. ([(LongForm)_180_Manufacturing_Data Science & Insights_Supply Chain_Demand Forecasting.pptx])

## Key Features

- **Model portfolio** — More than 100 models cover business units, plants, and P&L line items. ([(LongForm)_180_Manufacturing_Data Science & Insights_Supply Chain_Demand Forecasting.pptx])
- **Dynamic refresh** — Models rebuild monthly when new data arrives. ([(LongForm)_180_Manufacturing_Data Science & Insights_Supply Chain_Demand Forecasting.pptx])
- **Scenario planning** — Users can apply prebuilt economic scenarios or enter custom assumptions. ([(LongForm)_180_Manufacturing_Data Science & Insights_Supply Chain_Demand Forecasting.pptx])
- **Model governance** — Finance users can inspect fit, contribution, and training results and approve a model or let the system select one. ([(LongForm)_180_Manufacturing_Data Science & Insights_Supply Chain_Demand Forecasting.pptx])
- **Workforce planning** — The platform forecasts monthly manpower needs by plant. ([(LongForm)_180_Manufacturing_Data Science & Insights_Supply Chain_Demand Forecasting.pptx])

## Quantified Outcomes

- **50% lower error** — Forecast error fell from more than 10% MAPE to under 5% MAPE. ([(LongForm)_180_Manufacturing_Data Science & Insights_Supply Chain_Demand Forecasting.pptx])
- **18-month horizon** — Planning expanded from a three-month forecast. ([(LongForm)_180_Manufacturing_Data Science & Insights_Supply Chain_Demand Forecasting.pptx])
- **~70 plants** — EBITDA-level results became available at individual-plant granularity. ([(LongForm)_180_Manufacturing_Data Science & Insights_Supply Chain_Demand Forecasting.pptx])
- **18 external factors** — Market and economic indicators were incorporated into forecasting. ([(LongForm)_180_Manufacturing_Data Science & Insights_Supply Chain_Demand Forecasting.pptx])

## Business Value

The platform gave finance teams a longer and more granular view of demand, working capital, staffing, and financial performance while transferring operational ownership to the client. **Inference:** The case is relevant to manufacturers whose planning processes remain spreadsheet-bound and disconnected from market drivers. ([(LongForm)_180_Manufacturing_Data Science & Insights_Supply Chain_Demand Forecasting.pptx])
